Neither implies the other: that lemma charges each edge at its dyadic square's level with no covering term; the corollary charges a rectangle's variation at its short side and pays its maximum.

claims.summary: For h >= 0 constant on the columns of a mesh delta_0 and nonincreasing in x, B a union of cells, V_B = sum over the inner edges e of the boundary of B of delta_0 h(x_e) (x_e the column of e's B-cell) and A_B = sum over the rows of delta_0 (h(0) - h(rho_r)) (rho_r the right end of the row's run of B-cells starting at x = 0, 0 if none; h(1) = 0): (a) deterministically TV(h 1_B) <= 2 V_B + A_B; (b) on the event of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at delta_0, |D(h 1_B)| <= L sqrt N (log N)^(3/4) (2 V_B + A_B); (c) |D(h 1_B)| <= |D(h)| + L sqrt N (log N)^(3/4)(2 V'_(B^c) + A_(B^c)), V' read at the cells outside B.
claims.assessment: Working proof, passed with corrections in three passes of one medium reviewer (research/results/ultimate_matching_column_strips_20261018/review.txt), who checked (a)'s proof and the convention h(rho_r), (b), (c) and the High part's bound V_B <= 8(eps log N - 1)^(-1/4): along each run of B in a row the walls add up to at most the run's first value, which is the jump on the run's left edge of the boundary of B unless the run starts at x = 0; (b) is lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) after (a), no gain in order over it; (c) applies (b) to the complement.
claims.rationale: At (4,4) the walls of a one-height product chain are paid by the runs' left-end edges, whose increments are high where h is, so the part h >= W N^epsilon is at the target up to the variation along runs anchored at the side where h is largest.
claims.next_action: Bound the anchored part: split B into its left-justified part L_B and the rest, and charge the layers of h 1_(L_B), bounded by vertical lines and the staircase of the run ends, with the staircase's horizontal edges bounded by the variation across the boundary of B.

claims.summary: On the event of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, for every j with 1 <= j <= l_1, every cell function g on the mesh 2^(-j) and every partition of [0,1]^2 into rectangles R of cells with sides s_R <= l_R, M_R = max over R of g^+ plus max of g^-, Phi(R) = (2 log_2(2^j s_R) + 7)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N): |D(g)| <= L sqrt N sum_R Phi(R)(V^0_j(g 1_R) + 8(l_R + 4 s_R) M_R), V^0_j the cell variation of lem:tube-localized-discrepancy and L its constant; on the event of lem:loglog-mesh-deviation the same with sqrt(j + log log N) in place of sqrt(log N).
claims.assessment: Working proof, passed with corrections in three passes of one medium reviewer (research/results/ultimate_matching_column_strips_20261018/review.txt), whose first pass gave the one-step form adopted here and whose second checked the count of at most 2(l_R 2^k + 2) coarse cells and Phi: lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (b) on each rectangle at the coarse mesh 2^(-k), the largest dyadic at least the short side; the loglog form from that lemma's statement.
claims.rationale: Charges a cell function rectangle by rectangle at its short side's level; on product chains at (4,4) it gives the target for the part below W N^epsilon where the level strips are narrow.
claims.next_action: Use it on the low part of product chains with wide level strips only together with a bound on the middle-multiplicity pile; no direct next step.
